description.narrative: This joint program (JP) aims to enhance public and private sectorcollaboration around access to and sharing of data to improveagricultural efficiency and digital transformation in the agricultural sectorfor smallholder farmers, especially women and youth, leveragingtechnology-driven agricultural solutions to address challenges inproductivity, access to finance, inputs, markets, and managing theimpacts of climate change.The JP is designed to foster digital transformation within Tanzaniasagricultural sector aiming to enhance job creation, income generation,and livelihood resilience of smallholder farmers, especially women andyouth. The program will support the refinement of regulatory frameworksrelated to data governance, management, and interoperability, whileenforcing rigorous data security, protection standards, and privacynorms.A significant aspect of the JP involves the scaling up of 10 innovative agritechsthrough technical support and the provision of catalytic investmentto 3 agri-techs, aimed at improving the quality of digital solutions andscaling service delivery to smallholder farmers, especially women andyouth. Through agri-tech solutions and the enhanced capacity of 500government extension service providers (at least 30% women and 60%youth), farmers will improve their digital literacy and skills necessary toeffectively access and use digital agricultural services such as agri-inputs,market access, extension advisory, and financial services.The program anticipates directly benefiting at least 500,000 smallholderfarmers, including 300,000 women and 100,000 youth, who will gainaccess to enhanced digital services.
